title: Objective-C Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Print a greeting
entries.summary: printf is a C printing function. This Objective-C file can still use ordinary C code.
notes: Use a .m file so the compiler reads Objective-C.

entries.name: Keep a whole number
entries.summary: An int stores a whole number. %d tells printf where to place it.
notes: Match the print format to the number type.

entries.name: Use an NSString
entries.summary: NSString is an object holding text. The @ before the quotes makes an Objective-C string object.
notes: Plain "Asha" is C text, not an NSString object.

entries.name: Send a message to an object
entries.summary: Square brackets send a message. length asks a string for its length in UTF-16 units.
notes: String length is not always the number of visible symbols.

entries.name: Build a string with a value
entries.summary: stringWithFormat makes text with inserted values. %@ inserts an object description.

entries.name: Read an array item
entries.summary: NSArray stores object values in order. The first index is zero.
notes: Reading beyond the array count raises an exception.

entries.name: Find a value by key
entries.summary: NSDictionary connects keys to values. A text key can describe the data.
notes: Numbers in object collections need boxing such as @24.

entries.name: Choose a message
entries.summary: Objective-C keeps C if statements. The comparison produces a true-or-false result.
notes: Use == for a numeric equality test, not assignment =.

entries.name: Visit each object
entries.summary: Fast enumeration visits each object in a collection using for-in.
notes: Do not change the collection while enumerating it.

entries.name: Add an object
entries.summary: NSMutableArray allows changes such as adding an object.
notes: NSArray is read-only; use a mutable collection for changes.

entries.name: Recognise no object
entries.summary: nil means no object. Checking it can select a fallback message.
notes: Do not add nil to an NSArray; it expects an object.

entries.name: Compare the text itself
entries.summary: isEqualToString compares string contents. Pointer equality asks whether two references point to one object.
notes: Use text equality when you care about the letters, not object identity.
